clue.text: Independent young reporter in state should see development

indicators.note: the young reporter sits inside the word for state

parts.note: a nation is a state
a cub is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A junior journalist working abroad ought to witness how a country grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubation is the period in which something develops before it emerges, so it is a synonym of development.

clue.text: Line offered by Boris, panicked about answer?

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes round the abbreviation for answer
panicked suggests the letters of Boris thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A politician called Boris, flustered, delivers a line when asked for a response.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining points of equal pressure.

clue.text: First-class option

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, finest or select, as in a fine cut of meat
as a noun, a selection or alternative

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as an adjective for top quality and as a noun for something picked from alternatives.

clue.text: Disallow winning golf shot, getting concession

parts.note: to bar something is to forbid it
gaining means winning or acquiring
a chip is a short lofted golf shot

explanation.surface: An official rules out a successful golfing stroke, conceding the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargaining chip is something offered up in negotiation to win terms, a concession traded away.

clue.text: Law enforcement staff?

parts.note: staff means not personnel but a stick, the one a police officer carries

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as the people working in policing, but here it is a wooden staff: the police officer's club.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is the short club carried by British police officers, literally a stick used in enforcing the law.

clue.text: Coppice material seeing boost in Eire regularly

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of the words boost in Eire, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Irish woodland management gets a lift from new coppicing stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Osier is willow grown in coppiced beds whose flexible shoots are cut for basket-making.

clue.text: Group offering advice after son shows evidence of healing

indicators.note: the advice group comes after the abbreviation for son

parts.note: CAB is the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British charity giving free advice

explanation.surface: A counselling organisation follows up on a son who shows signs of recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: CAB, the Citizens Advice Bureau, is a UK network offering free legal and money advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the crust that forms over a wound as it mends, a visible sign of recovery.

clue.text: State agents must arrest a married bloke

indicators.note: arrest means hold, so the agency's letters hold the others inside them

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency, its staff are agents
bod is British slang for a person or bloke

explanation.surface: Intelligence officers are ordered to detain a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country in Southeast Asia, so a sovereign state.

clue.text: Repartee may be poor — at home with a case of gangrene!

parts.note: bad means poor in quality
in means at home

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, here of gangrene

explanation.surface: Banter might be in bad taste when the patient has gangrene at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, playful banter, the witty exchange that repartee also names.

clue.text: Establishment figure discovered in the RAF upset about head of government

parts.note: found means discovered

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the leading letter of government
upset says the letters of in the RAF are knocked into a new order
head of picks the first letter of government

explanation.surface: Someone found within the air force is upset about the leader of the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but belongs to the fodder: 'upset' rearranges all of IN THE RAF to INFATHER, and 'about' sets it round G.
explanation.definitionFit: A founding father establishes an institution or nation, a figure who set it up.

clue.text: Reputation of old party sure to be exposed

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle of sure

explanation.surface: An old political party is certain to have its reputation laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean the regard in which someone is held, as in being in good or bad odour.

clue.text: Soldiers will be this ignorant having lost one source of news

indicators.note: having lost means one letter is taken out of the word for ignorant

parts.note: uninformed means ignorant, lacking knowledge

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, here of news

explanation.surface: Troops are kept in the dark once they lose a source of information.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers wear regulation dress, so they are clothed in service kit, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Old account describing renovation of chair

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing around, so the abbreviation surrounds the rest
renovation means the letters of chair are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient story tells how a chair was restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means very old or antiquated, belonging to an earlier period.

clue.text: Treat with contempt as showing signs of exhaustion

definitions.meaning: to belittle or disparage someone, as a verb phrase
tired and worn out, as an adjective

explanation.definitionFit: To run down someone is to disparage them, and a run-down person is tired and weary.

clue.text: Imaginative log quietly growing

parts.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
P is piano, the musical term for quietly
rising means increasing or growing

explanation.surface: A log whose quiet growth is a sign of creative thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Enterprising means resourceful and inventive, showing initiative and fresh ideas.

clue.text: Summary with bank opening late must be just so

parts.note: a precis is a summary

indicators.note: late here means gone or departed, so the first letter of the word for bank is dropped

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A bank's summary report must be exact even if its doors open late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means former, departed: the opening R of RELY is gone, leaving ELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely means exactly, the same as 'just so' when agreeing that something is exactly right.

clue.text: Slight injury of a supporter is no different

parts.note: a bra supports, the classic crossword supporter

indicators.note: different means the letters of is no are put in another order

explanation.surface: A minor wound suffered by someone who backs a side is no different from any other.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a graze or scrape, a minor wound to the skin.

clue.text: Delighted, seeing European Commission interference

parts.note: static is crackling interference on a radio signal

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed to see Brussels meddling.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overjoyed, an intensified form of delighted.

clue.text: Plant that's traditionally seen at breakfast?

definitions.meaning: a folk name for bird's-foot trefoil, a yellow and orange flowered plant
the classic British cooked breakfast dish of fried rashers with fried eggs

explanation.definitionFit: Bird's-foot trefoil is nicknamed for its yellow and red flowers, and the same phrase names the traditional fried breakfast.

clue.text: Note story with universal setting

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a story can be a lie, a fib
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A short note relating a tale that suits everyone, with its background.
explanation.definitionFit: Milieu means surroundings or environment, the social setting in which something happens.

clue.text: Last of casualties has bare wound

indicators.note: picks the final letter of casualties

parts.note: naked means bare

explanation.surface: The final casualty has an uncovered injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' is not an injury but the past tense of wind, to twist and turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Snaked means twisted or meandered, as a road that wound through hills.

clue.text: Help for newsreader reporting traffic congestion?

indicators.note: reporting signals that the phrase is to be heard said, not seen written

parts.note: a line of jammed cars is an auto queue

explanation.surface: A news presenter's aid when broadcasting reports about traffic jams.
explanation.definitionFit: An Autocue is the screen displaying a script that a television presenter reads from, a teleprompter.

clue.text: Half of them will have trouble getting message

indicators.note: half of them takes its second pair of letters

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Half of the group will struggle to understand a communication.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message sent over the internet.

clue.text: European setting one boxer in bronze

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the boxer is placed inside the word for bronze

parts.note: tan is a bronze colour
Muhammad Ali is the crossword's favourite boxer

explanation.surface: A sculptor from the Continent casts a boxer's statue in bronze.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian is a person from Italy, so a European.

clue.text: Popular accountant stifled by banal complex

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: stifled means smothered, so the accountant is enclosed by the word for banal

parts.note: trite means banal or hackneyed
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A well-liked accountant is suffocated by a dull office complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate means elaborate and detailed, with many interlinking parts.

clue.text: Joint covering end of ski lift

indicators.note: covering means the joint's letters wrap around the other letter

parts.note: the hock is the joint in an animal's hind leg

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of ski

explanation.surface: A joint brace protects a skier on the ski lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoick is to haul or jerk something upwards, a British informal word for lift.

clue.text: Prison lift

definitions.meaning: British slang for jail or a police station

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the nick is a jail, and to nick something is to steal it.

clue.text: Where you may find children with no class?

definitions.text: Where you may find children with no class?

parts.words: Where you may find children with no class?
parts.note: no class means not in lessons, at break time, rather than lacking refinement

explanation.walkthrough: 'no class' suggests rough manners, but it means children out of lessons at break.
explanation.definitionFit: The school yard is where pupils play when they are not in lessons.
